column3: A command issued from God supports the divine side of the focus, though no human scheme is opposed.

The leaders deliberate over an alleged political threat, but the verse does not show a divine counter-decision.

It assures the believers that an enemy scheme will not harm them if they remain steadfast and mindful of God.

People may hide their night counsel from others but not from God, who encompasses what they secretly plan.
A group intends to mislead the messenger, but their scheme ultimately harms only themselves under divine protection.
The hypocrites try to deceive God, while God turns their attempted deception back upon them.
God restrains hands stretched out to harm the believers, showing hostile intent prevented by divine intervention.
The leading criminals in each town plot there, and God promises a humiliating recompense for their scheming.
It warns against feeling secure from God's plan, reinforcing that human security cannot escape divine design.
Pharaoh identifies an alleged concerted plot in the city to expel its people, an explicit political conspiracy.
God grants the wrongdoers respite while declaring His plan firm, closely echoing the focus's firm divine response.
The opponents plot to detain, kill, or expel the messenger, while God counter-plans and prevails.
The hypocrites plot what they fail to attain, a direct but less developed instance of hostile intent.
The harm-building is founded for disbelief, division, and ambush, an organized concealed design exposed by revelation.
When people plot against God's signs after mercy, God declares His planning swifter and His messengers record their plotting.
Jacob warns Joseph that his brothers may devise a scheme against him, introducing a direct family conspiracy.
The episode explicitly names the women's scheme, giving a clear but local instance of calculated deception.
Joseph identifies the women's scheme and seeks divine protection from it, directly joining human intrigue to divine deliverance.
God answers Joseph's prayer by turning their scheme away from him, a concrete divine counteraction to plotting.
Joseph states that his Lord knows the women's scheme, emphasizing divine knowledge of concealed planning.
It declares that God does not bring the scheme of betrayers to success, directly stating the failure of treacherous plans.
Earlier peoples plotted, but all planning belongs to God, who knows every soul's earning and determines the outcome.
Their plot is fully before God, yet it cannot overturn the order God has established.
God overturns the structure of earlier plotters' scheme from its foundations, bringing punishment from where they did not expect.
Those who plot evil are warned not to feel safe from God's plan and sudden punishment.
The opponents attempt to pressure the messenger away from revelation, an adversarial design restrained by divine protection.
Those seeking to drive the messenger from the land are warned that they would not remain long after him.
Pharaoh gathers his resources for a public confrontation, furnishing the setup for a deliberate hostile plan.
Pharaoh's magicians are told to gather and resolve their scheme before appearing in ranks, closely paralleling a fixed collective plan.
The magicians' scheme is declared unable to succeed, directly countering an organized hostile design.
They intend harm for Abraham, but God makes them the greatest losers, a concise reversal of human intent.
Pharaoh calls the magicians' belief a prearranged city plot, again presenting an explicit alleged conspiracy.
The plotters make a plan and God makes a plan while they do not perceive it, nearly duplicating the focus's structure.
It identifies the destructive end of the plotters' plan, completing the divine reversal of their conspiracy.
Pharaoh's household unknowingly takes in the child who will become their enemy and grief, a narrative reversal of hostile intent.
God repels the disbelievers in their rage without gain, showing a hostile campaign brought to nothing.
The weak identify the leaders' day-and-night plotting as the force that led them into disbelief.
Evil plotting rebounds only upon its own authors, directly stating the reversal of malicious schemes.
The evil plot surrounds only its own people, and the verse asks whether plotters expect anything but the established divine pattern.
They intend a plan against Abraham, but God makes them the lowest, a direct human-plan/divine-reversal pattern.
God protects the believer from the evils of what Pharaoh's people plotted, explicitly naming their plot and its failed effect.
It asks whether they seek a plot and answers that the disbelievers themselves will be caught in plotting, a close contextual parallel.
Secret counsels are held for sin, hostility, and disobedience, supplying a close counterpart to the focus's private consultation.
Those trusting in their fortresses are met by God from where they did not expect, overturning their calculated security.
The hypocrites plan to expel the believers from Medina, while the verse assigns true might to God, His messenger, and the believers.
God grants the deniers respite while declaring His plan firm, repeating a particularly close formulation of divine resolve.
Noah's people are described as plotting a great plot, a direct instance of entrenched collective opposition.
The opponents are explicitly said to be planning a plan, directly matching the human side of the focus.
God immediately answers that He too plans a plan, providing one of the closest verbal and structural parallels.
The elephant army's campaign is presented as an attack whose outcome is governed by God's decisive intervention.
God makes the elephant army's plan go astray, an explicit instance of a hostile plan being nullified.
